content: PHYLIP is a freely available software package designed for computational phylogenetics, which is the process of inferring evolutionary relationships and constructing phylogenetic trees. The name PHYLIP stands for PHYLogeny Inference Package. This package comprises 35 individual programs, all of which are portable and written in the C programming language. Precompiled versions of the software are available for various operating systems, including Windows (95/98/NT/2000/ME/XP), MacOS 8 and 9, MacOS X, and Linux. Comprehensive documentation is included with the package, providing detailed instructions for all the programs it contains. The software was developed by Joseph Felsenstein, a professor in the Department of Genome Sciences and the Department of Biology at the University of Washington in Seattle. PHYLIP implements several methods for phylogenetic analysis, including parsimony, distance matrix methods, and likelihood-based approaches. It also supports advanced techniques such as bootstrapping and the generation of consensus trees. PHYLIP is capable of analyzing a variety of data types, including molecular sequences, gene frequencies, restriction sites and fragments, distance matrices, and discrete characters. Each program within the package operates through a menu-driven interface, allowing users to select specific options and initiate computations. Input data is provided to the programs via text files, which must be prepared in a plain ASCII or Text Only format. Users can create these files using any standard text editor, but the files must not be saved in proprietary word processor formats. Some external sequence analysis tools, such as the ClustalW alignment program, are capable of generating data files in the PHYLIP format, making it easier to integrate with other software. By default, most PHYLIP programs look for an input file named infile. If this file is not found, the program prompts the user to specify the name of the input file. Output files are generated with names such as outfile and outtree. Phylogenetic trees written to the outtree file are formatted in the Newick format, which has been an informal standard for phylogenetic tree representation since 1986, agreed upon by developers of major phylogeny software packages.
